verdict.root_cause: fraud-detection is not failing requests; it is failing to reach its telemetry collector. From 17:04 onward it logs java.net.UnknownHostException for host 'otel-collector' on a fixed ~60s cadence, with one instance attributed to temporary name-resolution failure and a pause around 17:12-17:20 when resolution apparently worked [tr_e6c992444e81]. The traces are entirely OkHttp/OTel exporter frames with no application classes [tr_cd23ed25ab17]. The process keeps consuming order records past the alert time and its span error ratio (~0.4% mean, ~3% max) is an order of magnitude below its own baseline [tr_cd23ed25ab17][tr_e14805e67815][tr_3fa6a9b23618], and no change is recorded for fraud-detection or flagd [tr_bddf69fee5c9][tr_f56ce30cef2d]. The service is alive and complaining it cannot reach something: a connectivity/name-resolution break to otel-collector, whose visible symptom is a hole in fraud-detection's metrics.
verdict.reasoning: Application health is confirmed three ways: normal sequential record consumption with no app errors [tr_cd23ed25ab17], error ratio far below baseline with fraud-detection explicitly ruled out as error origin [tr_e14805e67815], and a 6-hour sample with no sustained departure [tr_3fa6a9b23618]. The only persistent fault is a DNS-layer unknown-host failure on a retry cadence rather than per request, which rules out business logic and per-request failure, and aborts before any connection attempt, ruling out a refusing/resetting collector [tr_e6c992444e81]. The service logs rather than falls silent, so not a freeze; the host resolved intermittently mid-window and no config or deploy is recorded [tr_bddf69fee5c9], so not a statically wrong value. The fix is restoring resolution/reachability, and there is nothing recorded to roll back.
open_questions: What actually tripped the 17:26:31 critical alert is unestablished — no error spike, throughput collapse or restart was seen; the exporter-induced metrics gap is only a hypothesis.

Blast radius of the DNS failure is unmeasured: no other service was checked for the same unknown-host error, and otel-collector itself was never queried, so the culprit could be the collector or cluster DNS.
All change-history windows start at onset and run forward, so the hours before 17:26:31 were never queried [tr_cd87ab1bf25f]; flagd was only ever checked in the change log, never in logs or metrics.

alternatives.root_cause: The otel-collector workload is gone or unhealthy, so its DNS name no longer resolves for any exporter.
alternatives.why_not: Entirely plausible and indistinguishable from the caller's side, but no dispatch ever touched otel-collector or any second service, so nothing supports it by result id.

alternatives.root_cause: fraud-detection's OTLP exporter endpoint names a collector host that does not exist in this environment.
alternatives.why_not: A permanently wrong hostname would fail continuously; resolution succeeded for roughly eight minutes mid-window and the first ~8 minutes were clean [tr_e6c992444e81], which fits intermittent resolution rather than a wrong value.

proposal.expected_effect: No action proposed, so no change should be observed. The expected continuing observation is the status quo: fraud-detection keeps consuming order records and emitting logs, its span error ratio stays at roughly 0.4% mean / 3% max, and java.net.UnknownHostException for host 'otel-collector' keeps appearing on a ~60s cadence in Loki until someone restores name resolution or network attachment between fraud-detection and otel-collector — an act outside this system's executor.
proposal.if_wrong: This abstention is wrong if the UnknownHostException is in fact caused by stale DNS state held inside the fraud-detection JVM or its container's resolver cache rather than by a cluster-DNS or collector-side break — in that case a container recreate would clear it and the per-minute exception line would stop within a couple of minutes. Two observations would show that: (a) another service in the same network resolving 'otel-collector' successfully during the same minutes, which would localise the fault to fraud-detection's own process/namespace, or (b) otel-collector being confirmed present and healthy. Neither was gathered — no other service was checked for the same unknown-host error and otel-collector was never queried. Equally, this abstention would be wrong in the other direction if the 17:26:31 critical alert turns out to be driven by something other than the metrics gap; the alert's actual trigger is unestablished, so no permitted action is known to address it.
proposal.risk: The risk of abstaining is that the telemetry gap persists and fraud-detection remains unobservable, so a later real failure in it would be invisible to metrics-based alerting; responders must treat its dashboards as untrustworthy until the exporter path is restored. The risk of the alternative I am declining — restart_service on fraud-detection — is concrete: its precondition ('the evidence points at process state rather than at a change') is not met, since the evidence names an unknown-host/name-resolution failure that occurs before any connection attempt [tr_e6c992444e81] and places the fault in the DNS or collector side, not in process state. A restart would discard in-process state, drop the Kafka consumer mid-stream for the recreate, and most likely leave the exporter failing on the same cadence, while destroying the one clean observation window we have of the fault. rollback_image and revert_config are not merely unwise but impossible: both require a prior image tag or configuration in change history, and the change log is empty for fraud-detection and for flagd across the entire queried window [tr_bddf69fee5c9][tr_f56ce30cef2d].
proposal.blast_radius: Nobody. No change is made, so no caller of fraud-detection sees anything. The consequence to communicate is informational: fraud-detection's metrics are expected to stay incomplete, and anyone relying on its Prometheus series — including whoever owns the 17:26:31 alert — should read its logs instead, where the service is demonstrably still consuming orders [tr_cd23ed25ab17]. The correct fix, restoring the fraud-detection-to-otel-collector network path, falls in the reconnect class, which this executor does not implement, so it needs a human on the cluster.

triage_judgement.reasoning: A critical alert on fraud-detection is not dismissible, and no open incident covers it. Its only upstream candidate is flagd, so a flag evaluation issue is the cheap prior, though evidence is absent.
